headline_marked: Starting at $1,999, [[Apple unveils iPhone Duo foldable]]
headline: Starting at $1,999, Apple unveils iPhone Duo foldable
summary: The first-ever foldable iPhone features a book-style design with a 7.6-inch inner display and a 5.4-inch outer screen, powered by the A20 Pro chip.
details: Apple has introduced the iPhone Duo, its first foldable smartphone. The device features a book-style design with a 7.6-inch inner display and a 5.4-inch outer screen, both supporting ProMotion and a peak brightness of 3,000 nits.

The inner screen uses a nano-texture finish to reduce glare and minimize the crease. For security, the device integrates Touch ID into the side button, while the FaceTime camera is placed beneath the inner display.

Built from grade 5 titanium, the iPhone Duo is powered by the A20 Pro chip. This 2-nanometre processor delivers up to 35% better sustained performance than the iPhone 17 Pro, supported by a custom vapour-chamber cooling system.

The foldable design enables new multitasking features in iOS 27, including Split View for running two apps side by side. Major apps like Netflix, Zoom, and Slack are already being adapted for the larger display.

The camera system consists of a 48-megapixel Fusion Main camera and a 48-megapixel ultra-wide camera. A 'Duo Preview' feature allows subjects to see live framing on the outer screen while shooting with the rear cameras.

The device uses a dual-battery design for extended playback, offering up to 31 hours of video playback on the inner screen and 44 hours on the outer screen. Wired charging can reach 50% in approximately 20 minutes.

Available in star white and night sky, the iPhone Duo comes in storage options from 256GB to 2TB. Prices start at $1,999 in the US, with pre-orders beginning October 16 and availability starting October 23 in over 70 countries.
The phone is eSIM-only worldwide and ships with iOS 27.1, featuring Apple's N1 networking chip for Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6.

headline: Chinmoy Krishna Das granted 5-hour parole to attend mother's cremation
summary: The former ISKCON leader was released from jail following the death of his 70-year-old mother, Sandhya Rani Dhar.
details: Former ISKCON leader Chinmoy Krishna Das Brahmachari was granted a five-hour parole today to attend the cremation of his mother, Sandhya Rani Dhar.
The Chattogram District Deputy Commissioner (DC) Mohammad Zahidul Islam Mia ordered the release at 2:30 PM following an application from the family.
Sandhya Rani Dhar, 70, passed away in Hathazari due to physical illness after receiving hospital treatment.
The cremation was scheduled to take place at the Pundrik Dham Temple in Hathazari upazila.
Additional security measures were implemented by the Hathazari Circle police to ensure the cremation process remained peaceful and to prevent any untoward incidents.
Chinmoy Das is currently in jail facing multiple cases, including a sedition charge and a murder case involving the death of advocate Saiful Islam Alif.
He was among 39 people charge-sheeted in the murder case of the lawyer, following clashes that broke out on November 26, 2024, after his bail was rejected.
While he has secured bail from the High Court in five other cases, he remains detained in the 관계로 remaining legal proceedings.
